event.title: France Enacts Social Media Ban for Children Under 15
event.canonical_title: France Enacts Social Media Ban for Children Under 15
event.summary: France's parliament has approved a bill that bans social media access for children under 15, making it the first European country to implement such a restriction. This legislation aims to protect minors from potential online harms associated with platforms like TikTok. The move is part of a broader trend in various countries to regulate children's access to social media.

timeline.title: Australian Teens Continue Online Activity Despite Under-16 Social Media Ban
timeline.summary: A recent report indicates that most Australian teenagers have managed to circumvent the government's ban on social media for those under 16, which was implemented three months ago. The Australian government has defended the ban, asserting its importance despite the findings showing minimal impact on teen usage.
key_facts: Most Australian teens still online three months after the under-16 social media ban.

timeline.title: Irish Regulator Engages TikTok on Reckless Driving Content Following Teen Tragedy
timeline.summary: Coimisiún na Meán, the Irish media regulator, is in contact with TikTok to gather information regarding the platform's handling of content related to reckless driving. This follows a tragic incident involving five teenagers and speeding the wrong way on a motorway, prompting concerns about the influence of 'joyriding' videos on social media.
key_facts: Coimisiún na Meán is liaising with TikTok.
The regulator seeks information on TikTok's response to reckless driving content.
Five teenagers were involved in a motorway incident involving speeding.

timeline.title: New Zealand Government Proposes Social Media Ban for Minors
timeline.summary: The New Zealand government plans to introduce a bill that would ban children under 16 from using social media, following a similar initiative in Australia. However, the proposal is facing opposition from some members of the ruling coalition who question its effectiveness.
key_facts: New Zealand government proposes a social media ban for those under 16.
The proposal is inspired by a similar ban in Australia.
Opposition exists within the ruling coalition regarding the effectiveness of the ban.

timeline.title: Meta Settles Social Media Addiction Lawsuits for $17 Billion
timeline.summary: Meta has reached a settlement of up to $17 billion to resolve multistate lawsuits regarding social media addiction. As part of the agreement, the company will implement changes to its platforms, including Facebook and Instagram. The settlement follows extensive negotiations led by state attorneys general amid mounting legal challenges for the tech giant.
key_facts: Meta settled for up to $17 billion regarding social media addiction lawsuits.

Negotiations were led by state attorneys general.
